Class Base32Codec

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.codec.transform.encoding.Base32Codec
All Implemented Interfaces:
Codec<byte[]>
public final class Base32Codec extends Object implements Codec<byte[]>
A byte-to-text-safe-byte transform using Base32 (RFC 4648 §6) or its "extended hex" variant (RFC 4648 §7). Base32 is larger than Base64 (8 characters per 5 bytes) but its alphabet has no lower-case letters and no symbols, which makes it safe for case-insensitive contexts — DNS labels, file names, and values a person will read aloud or type. It is the encoding used for TOTP secrets.

Output is upper-case with = padding, exactly as the RFC specifies. Decoding is strict but case-insensitive: a character outside the alphabet, misplaced padding, or a length that is not a multiple of eight is rejected with IllegalArgumentException.

Like Base64Codec, put it last in a chain. Instances are immutable and thread-safe.
